owner: Fable 5.1 lead session after the 2026-09-30 handoff

decode_census.method: A private copy of the pinned Starmap module printed one line for each DecodeCatalogPayload call. The copy never ships.

prototype_measurements.method: The private module copy returned the first complete decoded catalog for equal SHA-256 payload digests. The test source, assertions, full catalog, and 420-second deadline did not change. A replacement module file selected the copy. These runs measure the design only. They qualify no source.

decision.summary: Repair the repeated decode at its owner, Starmap pkg/catalogs, through an explicit bounded reuse scope. Starport opens the scope for one recovery activation.
reasons: One activation decodes one 26 MB payload 31 times through about 45 call sites in two repositories.
Canonical file inspection uses 2.86 of 25.5 activation CPU seconds. The stopped Starport semantic proof repair cannot supply enough margin alone.
A decoded catalog is immutable and its complete bytes determine it.
retained_checks: The scope key is the SHA-256 digest of the complete current payload bytes.
DecodeCatalogGeneration validates each generation, schema agreement, and membership evidence on each call.
The scope retains no failed decode, no partial diagnostic result, and no source observation.
The scope retains at most four catalogs and drops all of them at the last release.
A call without an open scope decodes in full. Restart and public inspection in another operation or process get no reuse.
The scope grants no authority and uses no timer. Each manifest, selection, identity, permission, and file check still runs.
decision.stopped_semantic_proof_worktree: The three unfinished files in /private/tmp/starport-recovery-canonical-semantic-20260930 stay preserved and unintegrated.

required_next: Merge the Starmap scope through review and native CI.
Pin it in Starport and open the scope in ActivateRecovery.
Repeat the unchanged full native pure and race test on the final source.
